newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan carries Dostum ceasefire offer to Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan carries Dostum ceasefire offer to Taleban.

text.p: Pakistani interior minister Naseerullah Babar conveyed a ceasefire offer from Afghanistan's Uzbek leader, General Abdul Rashid Dostum, to the fundamentalist Taleban militia on Sunday, Taleban sources said.

The sources said Babar passed on the proposal at a 30-minute meeting with senior Taleban leaders, including acting foreign minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous, at the Islamic movement's headquarters in the southern city of Kandahar.
Babar, who earlier flew from Islamabad to Dostum's base in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, told them the Uzbek chief had proposed that a ceasefire take effect at noon on Monday.
"We are thinking about it," one Taleban official, Mullah Abdul Jalil, told the Pakistan-based Afan Islamic Press (aip) agency.

Pakistan, which denies charges by the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani that it supports the mainly Pushtun Taleban, has been trying to avert fighting between the Sunni Moslem militants now holding Kabul and forces loyal to Dostum to the north.

A spokesman for Rabbani's military chief, Ahmad Shah Masood, said on Sunday that Dostum's troops were poised to push down the so-called new road from Bagram airbase, 60 km (40 miles) north of Kabul, but witnesses said the frontline there did not appear to have changed significantly.
